results.title: TGIIC proposes 27,500 acres for Telangana industries
results.description: Telangana : Telangana is planning large-scale land acquisition across the state to facilitate industrial development, with the process having begun in 22 districts. The Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) proposed the acquisition of more than 27,500 acres to the revenue department between December 2023 and June 2026. During the same period, it acquired more than […] Telangana : Telangana is planning large-scale land acquisition across the state to facilitate industrial development, with the process having begun in 22 districts. The Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) proposed the acquisition of more than 27,500 acres to the revenue department between December 2023 and June 2026. During the same period, it acquired more than 8,080 acres. Hyderabad region sees strong demand for industrial land Demand for industrial land has risen sharply in areas around Hyderabad. Despite high land prices, manufacturing, e-commerce and technology companies are competing for space in these locations. Investments are also coming from companies supplying components to defence and aerospace firms, besides those in pharmaceuticals, plastics and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). E-commerce companies are setting up large warehouses, while major firms are lining up to establish data centres. As a result, TGIIC is focusing on acquiring larger parcels in districts surrounding Hyderabad and those close to the state capital. The corporation is acquiring more than 10,000 acres in Vikarabad and Rangareddy districts alone, indicating the demand for land in the region. TGIIC hands over 2,400 acres to companies Between December 2023 and June 2026, more than 1,140 companies came forward to set up industries in Telangana. Together, they proposed investments of more than ₹94,000 crore. TGIIC handed over 2,400 acres to these companies. The firms that received land from the government have proposed creating employment for 85,000 people as part of their investment plans. Rangareddy district topped the list in industrial investments, followed by Nalgonda, Sangareddy, Medchal and Bhadradri Kothagudem. The pharmaceuticals and chemicals sectors attracted the highest investments, followed by solar and other renewable energy, industrial parks, IT buildings, food processing and engineering. District-wise land acquisition proposals District Proposed Acquired Vikarabad 5,051 acres 1,819 acres Rangareddy 5,011 acres 1,771 acres Sangareddy 4,161 acres 2,708 acres Medak 3,331 acres 137 acres Medchal-Malkajgiri 2,316 acres 428 acres Adilabad 2,062 acres — Nalgonda 818 acres — Narayanpet 562 acres — Mahabubnagar 416 acres — Yadadri Bhuvanagiri 344 acres — Average investment per unit rises nearly threefold The state received investment proposals worth ₹10,237 crore in the previous financial year. Between April and September this year, the government approved proposals worth ₹16,384 crore. A total of 1,172 industrial units have been approved so far this year, with the projects expected to create 30,511 jobs. In 2025-26, 2,163 units received the green light, with 51,029 jobs expected to be created. The average investment per unit rose from ₹4.7 crore last year to about ₹13.9 crore this year, nearly three times the previous figure. The Telangana government has also received another 1,178 proposals involving total investments of ₹79,032 crore. These proposals are yet to receive government approval and could create 87,863 jobs. ]]>

results.title: India Bat Against Pakistan in Asian Games Cricket Final; Teenager Kumkum Mohod Wins Archery Gold
results.description: India are batting at 58 for the loss of two wickets after four overs in the men's cricket gold medal match against Pakistan at the Asian Games , hours after 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod won India's first individual women's recurve gold. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was caught behind the wicket, walking back at 15 (9), while Sanju Samson was dismissed after scoring just two runs. Abhishekh Sharma is batting at 38 (12) and has been joined by skipper Shreyas Iyer at the crease for India, who were put in to bat after India won the toss and chose to bat first. The final is the first men's cricket meeting between India and Pakistan at the Asian Games. The captains did not shake hands at the toss, according to Cricinfo. India kept the same XI that beat Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the semifinal. Besides the openers, the batting has Sanju Samson, Iyer, Ishan Kishan, Tilak Varma and Shivam Dube, with Axar Patel, Washington Sundar, Ravi Bishnoi and Jasprit Bumrah as the bowling options. Pakistan, led by Sahibzada Farhan, also named an unchanged side from their semifinal win. Farhan is the batter to watch; he has two half-centuries in four T20I innings against India, averaging 38.75, and his nine sixes against them are the most by a Pakistan batter in T20 internationals. Samson, dismissed for seven in the semifinal, has a T20I strike rate below 100 against only Pakistan, although he has faced them just twice. Earlier in the day, Sri Lanka took the bronze medal by beating Bangladesh by 63 runs. Tharindu Ratnayake made 65 off 32 balls and took two wickets. Historic Archery Gold On the archery range, Kumkum Mohod beat South Korea's Oh Yejin 6-5 in a shoot-off after the final finished level at 5-5. Oh shot an 8 and Mohod answered with a 10. The teenager trailed 2-0 and 3-1, then levelled with a perfect 30 in the third set. After losing the fourth set, she forced the shoot-off with three 10s in the fifth. She had earlier beaten South Korea's world and Olympic champion Kang Chaeyoung 6-4 in the quarterfinal and China's Zhu Jingyi 6-2 in the semifinal. Her gold makes her the first Indian woman to win an individual recurve medal at the Asian Games. It also adds to India's only previous individual recurve medal, Tarundeep Rai's silver at the 2010 Guangzhou Games. On Friday, Mohod won women's recurve team gold with Ankita Bhakat and Kirti Sharma, beating South Korea 5-3, which was India's first Asian Games medal in that event. She also took mixed team silver with Dhiraj Bommadevara, after India lost 3-5 to China. India's medal tally stands at 77, with 17 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze, at the time of writing. results.title: Modi govt achieved historic milestone: HM Shah hails deportation of narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Turkey
results.description: New Delhi, Oct 3 (IANS) Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded the Modi government for securing the deportation of narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Turkey, describing it as a 'historic milestone'. HM Shah took to social media 'X' and said, "Modi govt has achieved a historic milestone by securing the deportation of hardened narco-trafficking kingpin Navpreet Singh from Türkiye." HM Shah said Singh had obtained Turkish citizenship using the fake identity of Navab Virk and continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine from Afghanistan to India. "Obtaining Turkish citizenship under the fake identity of Navab Virk, he had continued to smuggle heroin and methamphetamine to India from Afghanistan. Our agencies tracked him down, ripping apart veil after veil to unmask his true identity, and secured his deportation. Today he has been brought back to India and put behind bars in connection with cases involving drug trafficking and other crimes he is accused of. Congratulations to all the agencies for this success," he said. The Home Minister congratulated all the agencies involved in the operation and reiterated the government’s commitment to tackling drug trafficking. "Modi govt is committed to destroying every narco-cartel before Dec 2029," HM Shah added. Earlier in April, close aide of gangster Dawood Ibrahim and suspected drug trafficker Mohammad Salim Dola was brought back to India from Turkey. HM Shah had then said that the Narcotics Control Bureau had achieved a breakthrough in securing Dola’s return from Turkey. He said Dola’s arrest reflected the government’s resolve to bring narcotics fugitives and members of organised crime syndicates to justice. Earlier in May, the Delhi Police Special Cell, in coordination with the Central Bureau of Investigation had also extradited fugitive Prabhdeep Singh from Azerbaijan in connection with a major narcotics case involving the recovery of 358 kg of heroin. Prabhdeep, who had been absconding since 2023, was brought back to India from Baku by a three-member Special Cell team after completion of extradition formalities, police said. India and Turkey signed an extradition treaty in 2001, which came into force in June 2002. The agreement allows both countries to seek the transfer of fugitives wanted in terrorism and other serious criminal cases. In previous cases, Turkey has assisted India in deporting individuals linked to extremist networks, including suspected Islamic State operatives. Such cases are often coordinated through Interpol using Red Notices and other established procedures. --IANS jk/rad
